item.title: Lateral Elbow MWM
clinicalUse: Lateral elbow pain with painful grip and immediate improvement during glide
patientPosition: Sitting or supine with elbow positioned comfortably.
contact: Contact proximal forearm near elbow joint line using hands or belt.
forceDirection: Sustained lateral glide of forearm relative to humerus while patient performs pain-free grip or wrist movement.
dosage: 6–10 repetitions or repeated pain-free grips × 2–3 sets.
mistakes: Using MWM instead of tendon loading.
item.visualCue: Forearm lateral glide + grip → Immediate grip improvement = useful response.

subTechniques.name: Lateral Elbow Glide + Pain-Free Grip
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Reduce pain during gripping in selected lateral-elbow presentations when the glide produces an immediate change.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Sitting or standing with the elbow positioned exactly as in the painful grip test.
subTechniques.contact: Apply a sustained lateral glide across the elbow with a belt or manual contact while the forearm is stabilized.
subTechniques.direction: Maintain the glide while the patient performs the previously painful grip or wrist-extension task.
subTechniques.dosage: 6–10 repetitions or repeated pain-free grips for 2–3 sets if the response is clearly positive.
subTechniques.reassess: Pain-free grip strength and familiar functional grip task.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Use the painful grip itself as the comparable sign before and after every set.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Stop if the glide cannot make the movement comfortable.
